ei.subject: 영어2
ei.title: Microbes and Health — The Hidden Heroes Inside Us

fullPassage:
A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are clusters of bacteria in different parts of the body, such as on the surface or in the deep layers of the skin, in the mouth and the nose, and in the lungs and the stomach. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, reside in the gut. This may sound somewhat frightening, but these bacteria have a crucial and positive influence on our health. The first scientist who paid attention to these microbes in the gut and their importance was Ilya Mechinikov, who won the Nobel Prize in 1908 for his studies on the immune system. He was living in Paris in the late 19th century when thousands of people were suffering from cholera, a disease that was sweeping the European continent. As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease, which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. Remarkably, he didn't get sick. Intrigued, he decided to increase his sample size and recruited a colleague to do the same. The colleague didn't get sick either. But when he tested on another colleague, the poor man became critically ill and almost died. What made them react to the same disease in different ways? By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented it. After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were essential for human health, and that the right balance of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease. Sadly, this view was not widely accepted at the time and was eventually forgotten after Mechinikov died in 1916.

A decade later, antibiotics were discovered. Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. Moreover, people have come to see all germs as threats to good health, and as a result, they have done their best to keep their bodies clean of them. A war has been waged on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them. Unfortunately, this attitude has had harmful effects on health, resulting in a rise in allergies and immune deficiencies.

Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new light. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes. By occupying our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there. Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning. They also facilitate our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be rejected. Therefore, having insufficient germs or losing important ones leads to various health problems. Some microbes help the stomach digest some vegetables and milk. If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk, which eventually leads to an unbalanced diet and poorer health. Other bacteria help the body produce vitamins B and K, as well as important amino acids. Some microbes in the gut determine whether particular drugs are toxic to the liver and whether or not other drugs will work to combat a heart condition. Other microbes regulate the appetite hormone, which makes a person feel full or hungry. Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat. One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. Similarly, doing the reverse made the lean mouse gain weight.

Some researchers who have realized the crucial role of microbes are trying to apply this knowledge to cure people. Instead of using antibiotics, they have found that introducing or increasing the necessary germs that the person lacks can cure some diseases. For example, there were people who had a terrible form of diarrhea, so they had to go to the bathroom up to 20 times a day. These people had not been helped by antibiotic therapy. Researchers transplanted some of the good microbes from a healthy donor into these patients' guts. One day after they received their transplant, all their symptoms cleared up and the diarrhea vanished. They were essentially healthy again. The bacterial community in their own guts came to resemble the donor's bacterial community. Given this knowledge, nutritionists suggest the following ways to keep our guts healthy. One of the easiest ways to do this is through our food. Good microbes can be found in many of the foods we eat and whatever else gets to our mouths. By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, or choosing a diet packed with good, fresh nutrients, such as garlic, onions, and unprocessed grains rich in fiber, we can cultivate good microbes. Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food. Heavily processed foods such as frozen food, packaged snacks, and canned food not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals that damage the good microbes in our guts. Another way to increase beneficial microbes is to spend more time in nature. Places with diverse life forms, such as woods, beaches, parks, or even small farms and gardens, are abundant with diverse bacteria that germ-free urban environments lack. In addition, we should use antibiotics wisely; we must use them much less frequently. Although antibiotics play a crucial role in keeping us healthy by eliminating dangerous germs, they cannot tell good bacteria from bad ones. Therefore, whenever we use antibiotics, we inevitably damage beneficial bacteria as well as the harmful bacteria that we want to get rid of. If we can affect microbes and they can affect our bodies, it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.

questions.passage: A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are clusters of bacteria in different parts of the body, such as on the surface or in the deep layers of the skin, in the mouth and the nose, and in the lungs and the stomach. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, (A)[reside / travel] in the gut. This may sound somewhat (B)[frightening / encouraging], but these bacteria have a (C)[crucial / trivial] and positive influence on our health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가장 많은 수의 박테리아, 약 100조 개가 장에 거주한다. 이것이 다소 무섭게 들릴 수 있지만, 이 박테리아는 건강에 중대한 긍정적 영향을 미친다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① reside(거주하다) — frightening(무서운) — crucial(중대한): 박테리아가 장에 '살고', 100조라는 숫자가 '무섭게' 들릴 수 있으나 '중대한' 긍정적 영향이 있다는 맥락. ❌ travel(이동하다)은 거주의 맥락과 불일치. ❌ encouraging(격려하는)은 '무섭게 들리지만'의 역접과 불일치. ❌ trivial(사소한)은 positive influence와 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: reside = live, dwell (거주하다). crucial = essential = vital (중대한, 필수적인)

questions.passage: As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease, which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. Remarkably, he didn't get sick. (A)[Intrigued / Disappointed], he decided to increase his sample size and (B)[recruited / dismissed] a colleague to do the same. The colleague didn't get sick either. But when he tested on another colleague, the poor man became (C)[critically / mildly] ill and almost died.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 흥미를 느낀 그는 표본 크기를 늘리기로 하고 동료를 모집했다. 하지만 또 다른 동료에게 실험했을 때, 그 사람은 심각하게 아팠다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② Intrigued(흥미를 느낀) — recruited(모집한) — critically(심각하게): 아프지 않은 결과에 '흥미를 느꼈고', 동료를 '모집'했으며, 다른 동료는 '심각하게' 아팠다. ❌ Disappointed(실망한)는 '안 아팠으니 실망'이 아닌 문맥. ❌ dismissed(해고한)는 실험을 위해 부르는 맥락과 반대. ❌ mildly(가볍게)는 'almost died'와 모순.
det.tip: intrigued = curious, fascinated (흥미를 느낀). recruit = enlist, hire (모집하다)

questions.passage: Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new light. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly (A)[dependent / independent] upon the well-being of these (B)[numerous / scarce] and diverse microbes. By (C)[occupying / abandoning] our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 건강은 이러한 수많은 다양한 미생물의 안녕에 놀라울 정도로 의존적이다. 우리 몸을 먼저 점유함으로써 해로운 세균이 자라는 것을 막는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ dependent(의존적인) — numerous(수많은) — occupying(점유하는): 건강이 미생물에 '의존'하고, '수많은' 다양한 미생물이 먼저 '점유'해서 보호한다. ❌ independent(독립적인)는 의존 관계 설명과 반대. ❌ scarce(희귀한)는 thousands of species와 불일치. ❌ abandoning(버리는)은 보호 기능과 반대.
det.tip: dependent upon = relying on (~에 의존하는). occupy = take up space (점유하다, 차지하다)

questions.passage: Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that ①<u>infect</u> wounds, cause ②<u>deadly</u> diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. Moreover, people have come to see all germs as ③<u>threats</u> to good health, and as a result, they have done their best to keep their bodies clean of them. A war has been ④<u>avoided</u> on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 항생제는 상처를 감염시키고 치명적인 질병을 일으키는 유해 세균을 죽이는 수단을 제공했다. 사람들은 모든 세균을 건강에 대한 위협으로 보게 되었고, 미생물에 대한 전쟁이 벌어졌다(waged).
det.analysis: ❌ ④ avoided(피한) → waged(벌인)가 적절. 미생물에 대해 전쟁을 '피한' 것이 아니라 '벌인' 것이 문맥에 맞음. 사람들이 거의 한 세기 동안 미생물을 죽이려 했다는 뒤 문장과 연결됨. ✅ ①②③은 원문 그대로 적절.
det.tip: wage a war = 전쟁을 벌이다 ↔ avoid a war = 전쟁을 피하다. wage(동사): 전쟁/캠페인을 벌이다

questions.passage: Some researchers who have realized the crucial role of microbes are trying to apply this knowledge to cure people. Instead of using antibiotics, they have found that introducing or increasing the necessary germs that the person lacks can cure some diseases. For example, there were people who had a terrible form of diarrhea, so they had to go to the bathroom up to 20 times a day. These people had not been helped by antibiotic therapy. Researchers transplanted some of the good microbes from a healthy ①<u>donor</u> into these patients' guts. One day after they received their transplant, all their ②<u>symptoms</u> cleared up and the diarrhea ③<u>intensified</u>. They were essentially ④<u>healthy</u> again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 건강한 기증자로부터 좋은 미생물을 이식했다. 이식 후 하루 만에 모든 증상이 사라지고 설사가 사라졌다(vanished). 그들은 본질적으로 다시 건강해졌다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ intensified(심화되었다) → vanished(사라졌다)가 적절. 이식 후 설사가 '심화'된 것이 아니라 '사라졌다'는 것이 긍정적 결과의 맥락에 맞음. ✅ ①②④는 원문 그대로 적절.
det.tip: vanish = disappear = go away (사라지다) ↔ intensify = get worse (심화되다)

questions.passage: By occupying our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there. Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain ①<u>unaffected</u> by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning. They also ②<u>facilitate</u> our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be ③<u>accepted</u>. Therefore, having ④<u>insufficient</u> germs or losing important ones leads to various health problems.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 우리 몸을 먼저 점유하여 해로운 세균의 성장을 막는다. 건강한 박테리아 군집을 가진 사람들은 약간 감염된 음식에 영향을 받지 않을 수 있다. 미생물은 면역 체계를 촉진하여 좋은 물질과 거부(rejected)되어야 할 해로운 물질을 구별한다. 불충분한 세균은 건강 문제를 초래한다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ accepted(수용된) → rejected(거부된)가 적절. 해로운 물질은 '수용'되는 것이 아니라 '거부'되어야 한다는 문맥. 면역 체계가 좋은 물질은 허용하고 해로운 물질은 거부하는 기능을 한다. ✅ ①②④는 원문 그대로 적절.
det.tip: reject = refuse, turn away (거부하다) ↔ accept = receive, welcome (수용하다). facilitate = help, promote (촉진하다)

questions.passage: A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are __________ of bacteria in different parts of the body, such as on the surface or in the deep layers of the skin, in the mouth and the nose, and in the lungs and the stomach. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, reside in the gut. This may sound somewhat frightening, but these bacteria have a crucial and positive influence on our health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 생물들은 몸의 여러 부분에 있는 박테리아의 집단(무리)이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② clusters: 'clusters of bacteria' = 박테리아의 무리/집단. 피부, 입, 코, 폐, 위 등 다양한 곳에 모여 사는 박테리아 군집을 의미. ❌ ① layers(층)는 bacteria와 어울리지 않음. ❌ ③ samples(표본)은 과학적 채취 맥락. ❌ ④ traces(흔적)는 소량이라는 뉘앙스.
det.tip: cluster = group, bunch (무리, 집단). clusters of bacteria = 박테리아 군집

questions.passage: Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. Moreover, people have come to see all germs as threats to good health, and as a result, they have done their best to keep their bodies clean of them. A war has been waged on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them. Unfortunately, this attitude has had harmful effects on health, resulting in a rise in allergies and immune __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이러한 태도는 건강에 해로운 영향을 끼쳐, 알레르기와 면역 결핍의 증가를 초래했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ deficiencies: 'immune deficiencies' = 면역 결핍. 미생물을 무분별하게 죽인 결과 면역 체계가 약해졌다는 맥락. ❌ ① responses(반응)는 중립적 의미. ❌ ② enhancements(강화)는 긍정적 의미. ❌ ④ advantages(이점)는 해로운 효과와 반대.
det.tip: deficiency = lack, shortage (결핍, 부족). immune deficiency = 면역 결핍

questions.passage: Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food. Heavily processed foods such as frozen food, packaged snacks, and canned food not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals that damage the good microbes in our guts. Another way to increase beneficial microbes is to spend more time in nature. Places with diverse life forms, such as woods, beaches, parks, or even small farms and gardens, are __________ with diverse bacteria that germ-free urban environments lack.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다양한 생명체가 있는 숲, 해변, 공원 등은 무균 도시 환경에 없는 다양한 박테리아로 풍부하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① abundant: 'abundant with diverse bacteria' = 다양한 박테리아가 풍부한. 자연 환경이 도시와 달리 다양한 박테리아가 많다는 맥락. ❌ ② contaminated(오염된)는 부정적 뉘앙스. ❌ ③ incompatible(양립할 수 없는)은 문맥 부적합. ❌ ④ unfamiliar(익숙하지 않은)는 의미 불일치.
det.tip: abundant = plentiful, rich (풍부한). be abundant with = ~이 풍부하다

questions.passage: A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are clusters of bacteria in different parts of the body, such as on the surface or in the deep layers of the skin, in the mouth and the nose, and in the lungs and the stomach. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, reside in the gut. This may sound somewhat frightening, but these bacteria have a <u>crucial</u> and positive influence on our health.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>crucial</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이 박테리아는 우리 건강에 결정적인 긍정적 영향을 미친다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② essential: crucial = essential = 필수적인, 결정적인. 박테리아가 건강에 매우 중요한 역할을 한다는 맥락. ❌ ① minimal(최소한의)은 반대 의미. ❌ ③ temporary(일시적인)은 무관. ❌ ④ optional(선택적인)은 필수의 반대.
det.tip: crucial = essential = vital = critical = indispensable (결정적인, 필수적인)

questions.passage: Antibiotics have saved <u>countless</u> lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>countless</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 항생제는 셀 수 없이 많은 생명을 구했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ innumerable: countless = innumerable = 셀 수 없이 많은. ❌ ① limited(제한된)은 반대 의미. ❌ ② measurable(측정 가능한)은 뜻이 다름. ❌ ④ occasional(가끔의)은 빈도를 의미.
det.tip: countless = innumerable = numerous = a great many (셀 수 없이 많은)

questions.passage: By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, or choosing a diet packed with good, fresh nutrients, such as garlic, onions, and unprocessed grains rich in fiber, we can <u>cultivate</u> good microbes. Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>cultivate</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 유익한 박테리아가 포함된 음식을 먹으면 좋은 미생물을 기를 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ foster: cultivate = foster = nurture = 기르다, 육성하다. 좋은 음식을 통해 미생물을 키운다는 맥락에서 '육성하다'가 적절. ❌ ① eliminate(제거하다)은 반대. ❌ ② identify(확인하다)는 다른 맥락. ❌ ③ consume(소비하다)은 먹는 것이지 기르는 것이 아님.
det.tip: cultivate = foster = nurture = grow (기르다, 육성하다). cultivate는 농업(경작)뿐 아니라 비유적으로 '키우다'의 뜻도 있음.

questions.passage: By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented it. After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were <u>essential</u> for human health, and that the right balance of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 essential과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 장 박테리아가 인간 건강에 필수적이라는 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② unnecessary: essential(필수적인)의 반의어 = unnecessary(불필요한). ❌ ① fundamental(근본적인)은 유의어. ❌ ③ significant(중요한)은 유의어. ❌ ④ beneficial(유익한)은 다른 차원의 긍정적 의미.
det.tip: essential(필수적인) ↔ unnecessary(불필요한). essential = indispensable, vital

questions.passage: Although antibiotics play a crucial role in keeping us healthy by eliminating dangerous germs, they cannot tell good bacteria from bad ones. Therefore, whenever we use antibiotics, we <u>inevitably</u> damage beneficial bacteria as well as the harmful bacteria that we want to get rid of.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 inevitably와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 항생제를 사용할 때마다 유익한 박테리아도 불가피하게 손상시킨다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ optionally: inevitably(불가피하게, 필연적으로)의 반의어는 optionally(선택적으로), 즉 피할 수 있고 선택의 여지가 있다는 의미. ❌ ① accidentally(우연히)는 '의도 없이'의 의미. ❌ ② simultaneously(동시에)는 시간 관련. ❌ ④ continuously(계속해서)는 빈도/기간 관련.
det.tip: inevitably(불가피하게, 필연적으로) ↔ optionally(선택적으로), avoidably(피할 수 있게). inevitable = unavoidable

questions.passage: Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new <u>light</u>. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>light</u>가 다음 글에서 사용된 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 과학자들이 미생물과 인체 사이의 관계를 새로운 관점(시각)에서 보기 시작했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ '이 발견은 이전 연구에 새로운 light를 비추었다' → light = 관점, 시각, 조명(비유적). in a new light = 새로운 관점에서. ❌ ① '방 안에 light가 충분했다' → 빛, 조명(물리적). ❌ ② '그녀는 light한 색상의 드레스를 입었다' → 밝은, 연한(색). ❌ ③ '가방이 매우 light했다' → 가벼운(무게).
det.tip: in a new light = 새로운 관점에서. light의 다의어: ① 빛 ② 밝은 ③ 가벼운 ④ 관점/시각

ch: There was enough light in the room to read.
She wore a dress in light colors.
The bag was very light to carry.
This discovery shed new light on previous research.

questions.passage: Some microbes in the gut determine whether particular drugs are toxic to the liver and whether or not other drugs will work to combat a heart condition. Other microbes regulate the appetite hormone, which makes a person feel full or hungry. Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat. One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight.
questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어를 본문에서 고르시오.

"to control or adjust something so that it operates correctly or within certain limits"

det.korean: 무언가를 올바르게 작동하거나 특정 범위 내에서 작동하도록 조절하는 것
det.analysis: ✅ ② regulate: '올바르게 작동하도록 조절하다' = regulate. 미생물이 식욕 호르몬을 조절한다는 맥락. ❌ ① transplanting(이식하는)은 옮기는 행위. ❌ ③ combat(싸우다)은 대항하는 행위. ❌ ④ determine(결정하다)은 판단/확인의 의미.
det.tip: regulate = control, adjust, manage (조절하다, 규제하다). regulate는 '일정하게 유지하다'의 뉘앙스.

questions.passage: He was living in Paris in the late 19th century when thousands of people were suffering from cholera, a disease that was sweeping the European continent. As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease, which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. Remarkably, he didn't get sick. Intrigued, he decided to increase his sample size and recruited a colleague to do the same.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하여 쓰시오.

Mechinikov was ( nature ) driven to study cholera because he was a scientist.

det.ref: [원문] As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease. [해석] 과학자로서 메치니코프는 자연스럽게 이 질병을 연구하게 되었다.
det.tip:
💡 nature(명사) → naturally(부사). 동사 driven을 수식하므로 부사형이 필요하다.
⚠️ natural(형용사) vs. naturally(부사) — 동사/형용사를 수식할 때는 부사!

questions.passage: They also facilitate our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be rejected. Therefore, having insufficient germs or losing important ones leads to various health problems. Some microbes help the stomach digest some vegetables and milk. If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk, which eventually leads to an unbalanced diet and poorer health.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하여 쓰시오.

Microbes help our immune system by ( distinguish ) between good and harmful substances.

det.ref: [원문] They also facilitate our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be rejected. [해석] 우리 몸에 허용되어야 할 좋은 물질과 거부되어야 할 해로운 물질을 구별함으로써 면역 체계를 촉진한다.
det.tip:
💡 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. by + V-ing = '~함으로써'
⚠️ distinguish between A and B = A와 B를 구별하다

questions.passage: After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were essential for human health, and that the right __________ of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease. Sadly, this view was not widely accepted at the time and was eventually forgotten after Mechinikov died in 1916.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리 몸 안의 미생물의 올바른 균형이 질병 예방에 도움이 될 수 있다고 깨달았다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ balance: 'the right balance of microbes' = 미생물의 올바른 균형. 일부 박테리아는 콜레라를 촉진하고 일부는 억제한다는 발견 맥락에서 '균형'이 적절. ❌ ① elimination(제거)은 모든 미생물을 없애는 것. ❌ ② absence(부재)은 없음. ❌ ④ mutation(변이)은 유전자 변화.
det.tip: balance = equilibrium (균형). the right balance of = ~의 올바른 균형

questions.passage: If we can affect microbes and they can affect our bodies, it makes little sense to talk about the two __________. Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리가 미생물에 영향을 줄 수 있고 미생물이 우리 몸에 영향을 줄 수 있다면, 둘을 따로 이야기하는 것은 의미가 없다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② separately: 'talk about the two separately' = 둘을 따로 이야기하다. 미생물과 우리 몸이 상호 영향을 미치므로 분리해서 생각하면 안 된다는 결론. ❌ ① simultaneously(동시에)는 오히려 함께 다루는 의미. ❌ ③ frequently(자주)는 빈도의 문제. ❌ ④ scientifically(과학적으로)는 방법론의 문제.
det.tip: separately = apart, individually (따로, 별도로). make little sense = 의미가 거의 없다, 말이 안 되다
